newsitem.title: USA: U.S. government halts Harvard Russian contract - paper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. government halts Harvard Russian contract - paper.

text.p: The U.S. government suspended a $14 million contract with Harvard University saying two employees used information from a government-funded project in Russia to profit from personal investments in Russian securities, The Boston Globe reported on Wednesday.

The U.S. Agency for International Development, in a letter sent to the university, said a preliminary investigation found the Harvard Institute for International Development's general director in Moscow, Jonathan Hay, and the project director, Andrei Shleifer, "abused the trust of the United States government by using personal relationships, on occasion, for private gains," the newspaper said.

The contract is the last instalment of a $57 million grant awarded to the institute, which since 1992 has been helping Russian officials privatise government operations and change the country's legal system and its capital markets.

The federal agency said Hay "used resources financed by USAID to support the private investment activities" of Shleifer's wife, Nancy Zimmerman, including "buying and selling Russian bonds, tracking deposits and withdrawals from the investments' Russian bank accounts, consulting about tax aspects of the investments and possible additional investment opportunities," the Globe said.

Michael Butler, a Washington lawyer for Hay and Shleifer told the Globe the USAID's letter is "wrong in its conclusions, wrong in its assumptions and inaccurate in its facts and foolish in its rhetoric."
Neither Butler, nor Harvard University spokesmen could be reached immediately for comment on the report.
